title: Register changes that record the reviewed E01-D result, V2-S3-005-PR1
description: What V2-S3-005-PR1 changed in the register to record the result of part E01-D of V2-E01: every register change with its value before and after, the finding each answers, and the review artifacts the changes rest on. The run, 20261006-e01-d-1, executed on 2026-10-06 in V2-S3-004-PR2, and its independent review merged with that change. That change registered no claim. The first Sprint 3 collective review found the omission, and this ledger is the correction, written on 2026-10-07. It is the sixth ledger written after v1.0.0 was released, and like the five before it, it is not part of the pack that release was cut over: the evidence index undoes it, with the other post-release ledgers, to recompute that pack. It adds one claim, certified at C2 on the one record it adds with it. It appends a dated note to the limitation of two planned claims and moves neither status. It replaces one clause in what the second static run's claim does not establish, and it replaces one surface reason. It runs no part of E01, changes no file of a run, a freeze record, or a review record, raises and closes no blocker, declares no freeze, states no release, and edits no dated record and no earlier ledger.

claim.statement: In one run on 2026-10-06, on the docker-desktop provider, on one cluster with one node, the release rendered from the unmodified V1 synchronous reference contract on the local-docker-desktop binding was accepted into Git at commit ad725905a7838e8210e54a29de7913bc0c7c49e5, was reconciled by Argo CD into Kubernetes, and answered one completion request through the InferOps API with HTTP 200 and one choice whose assistant message is not empty, with the real runtime and the real model that the generated values name. The run answers the criteria E01-AC8, E01-AC9, and E01-AC10 that freeze revision 3 registers for E01-D, and each holds.
claim.limitation: Runtime, C2, about one run, 20261006-e01-d-1, at one commit, on one provider, docker-desktop, on one cluster with one node on Kubernetes v1.36.1, with one contract, one binding, one API replica, one runtime replica, and one completion request. The model cache was filled from a seed image before the deployment. The API image was built on the host, and the operator supplied its digest as one Helm parameter and applied the Application and its project. The same images had started on the node about two minutes earlier, so the deployment is a warm start. No runner and no coded analysis exist for E01-D: the automated assistant session that drove the run applied the registered rules. The review of the result is a record of a separate session of the same assistant, and no person and no outside party reviewed the result. The run did not observe the network. The clause of E01-AC10 about strings of eight characters or more rests on the second static run and on three tests, and is not computed over the live Application. The pod status reports the API container's image under another digest than the one the run supplied, and the read of the node that reconciles the two is not a registered step. Registration, 2026-10-07: the run executed and was reviewed on 2026-10-06 in V2-S3-004, and that change registered no claim. The first Sprint 3 collective review found the omission, and V2-S3-005 added this claim after the review record had merged. The run, its files, its outcome, its evidence level, and its review record are unchanged, and no part of E01 ran again.
claim.doesNotEstablish: That a second request is answered; behaviour on another provider, Kubernetes version, node count, storage class, workload shape, contract, or binding; that Argo CD applies a later commit of main; a caller outcome from a sync state, a health state, pod readiness, or a replica count; that the acquisition hook downloads the model into an empty claim; latency, throughput, capacity, availability, or behaviour under overload; reliability under failure, high availability, or tolerance of the loss of a pod, a node, a zone, or a region; that a service-level objective is met; representative evidence, C3, or operational evidence, C4; a cost, a saving, a return on investment, or a business effect; that a person reviewed the result; or production readiness.

evidenceRecords.summary: On 2026-10-06 part E01-D of V2-E01 ran once, as freeze revision 3 registers it, at the merged commit ad725905a7838e8210e54a29de7913bc0c7c49e5, on the docker-desktop provider. Argo CD reconciled the generated release of that commit into one cluster of one node, the run sent one completion request through the InferOps API, and the response was HTTP 200 with one choice and an assistant message of six characters. E01-AC8, E01-AC9, and E01-AC10 hold, and the outcome is PASSED. The run was registered on 2026-10-07, after its independent review merged.

The committed release was rendered before the run, in an earlier change.

The Docker Desktop cluster, one node, desktop-control-plane, Kubernetes v1.36.1, with the default storage class standard.
Step P5 created the namespace inferops-release and the model cache claim. The cleanup destroyed both.

One replica of the API Deployment, from an image that step P4 built on the host at the executing commit and loaded into the node. It answered the readiness request and the one completion request through a kubectl port-forward to its Service.
One replica of the runtime Deployment. The container status reports the image digest that the generated values name.

Qwen3-1.7B-Q8_0.gguf, mounted at the generated model revision. The verify-model init container ended with exit code 0, and the response names the generated model identifier. Step P6 filled the model cache claim from a seed image before the deployment.
tools/reconciliation_evidence and tools/desired_state_provenance, run in step D6. They wrote the reconciliation record over five samples and the provenance of the reported commit.

workload.description: One fixed chat completion request, with the one user message 'Reply with the single word: ready', sent once by the driver with no retry. The generated text is not kept. The run records its length.

One Kubernetes cluster of one node, desktop-control-plane, server v1.36.1, node kernel 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2, 12 processors and 10186220Ki of memory, CPU only. One API replica and one runtime replica in the namespace inferops-release. Argo CD v3.5.3, core install, in the namespace argocd. 2026-10-06. Freeze revision 3 names this environment, and step P3 read the thirteen attributes that the run compares with it.

measurement.method: The driver wrote the HTTP status that curl printed, the number of choices, and the length of the first assistant message to completion.json, and wrote the Application and the pods as kubectl returned them. The session that drove the run then applied the verification rules that freeze revision 3 registers to those files.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The release rendered from the unmodified reference contract, accepted into Git and reconciled by Argo CD, produces at least one real successful completion: HTTP 200, with at least one choice whose assistant message is not empty.

The deployed identities verify against the release: the desired-state revision Argo CD reports as synced holds the generated release; the release records the contract, binding, and values digests, and they match their sources and the values file; the running runtime container's image digest is the generated runtime.image.digest; the model revision the runtime reads is the generated model.revision; and the API serves the model under the generated model.identifier.

No claim-relevant workload intent is written by hand after rendering: no hand-written value and no operator-supplied parameter of the release restates or overrides claim-relevant workload intent; the release takes its values from the generated values file, from the hand-written values of the Argo CD Application, and from one operator-supplied Helm parameter, api.image.digest, over the chart's own defaults, and from no other source; admit_manual_values admits those hand-written values, with that parameter, beside the generated values with no finding; and no string in them contains a workload-intent generated value of eight characters or more.

results.statement: The one request of step D5 returned HTTP status 200. The response holds one choice, and its assistant message has a length of 6. The run sent one request and no retry.

Argo CD reported Synced and Succeeded at the executing commit. The provenance resolved from that commit gives the release identifier and the values digest that freeze revision 3 names. The runtime container's image identity ends with the generated digest, the model volume is mounted at the generated revision with verify-model at exit code 0, and the response names the model qwen3-1-7b-q8-0.

The Application named exactly the one generated values file, the hand-written values of the committed manifest, and one parameter, api.image.digest, with the digest of step P4. The three selected tests passed. The clause about strings of eight characters or more rests on the second static run and was not computed over the live Application.

limitations: One run, on one provider, on one cluster with one node, with one contract, one binding, one API replica, one runtime replica, and one completion request.

No runner and no coded analysis exist for E01-D. The automated assistant session that wrote the driver started it and applied the registered verification rules to the files. The run manifest states each compared value.
The review of the result is a record of a separate session of the same automated assistant. It is not a review by a person or by an outside party. The review record states its own limits.
The driver is not a pinned input of the freeze record. driver.txt holds it as it ran.
The model cache claim was filled from a seed image in step P6, before the deployment. The run did not observe the network, and it does not establish whether the acquisition hook downloaded anything.
The API image was built on the host and loaded into the node. The operator supplied its digest as one Helm parameter, and the operator applied the Application and its project.
The same images had started on the same node in step P6, about two minutes before the deployment. The 18 seconds from the apply to both rollouts is a warm start.

The clause of E01-AC10 about strings of eight characters or more is not computed over the live Application. It rests on the second static run, 20261003-e01-abc-1, and on three tests. No step ran the admission check over the hand-written values with the parameter merged in.
The model revision is verified by configuration and by content. Nothing reads the revision from the model file.

The pod status reports the API container's image under another digest than the one the run supplied. A read of the node after the cleanup listed both digests for one image identifier. That read is not a registered step, and its output is not in the run directory.

transcript.txt is the driver's output after five transformations, which the review record and the validation record list. commands.txt is not the exact commands, and driver.txt holds them. The output of three commands of step P3, the response body, and the readiness body are under a directory that Git ignores, and they are not committed.
In environment.json, the read values of the provider and of the kube context are literals of the driver. The target verification of the procedures, in the transcript, is the evidence for both.
The times are the host's clock and the cluster's clock. No repository file proves them.

findings.observation: The first Sprint 3 collective review, on 2026-10-06, finding F1: V2-S3-004 produced the frozen E01-D run and its review record and did not reconcile the register. The register held no claim and no evidence record for 20261006-e01-d-1, and a test required that absence. The review found the freeze inputs, the raw run, the result classification, and the review record sound, and stated that the finding justifies no repeated run.
findings.resolution: One claim, with one record at C2, is added. The ledger references the review record of the run, which merged before this change. No part of E01 ran again, and no file of the run, of a freeze record, or of a review record changed.

findings.observation: Two planned claims carry a limitation that describes the state before the E01-D run: one says that every real run deployed from a feasibility manifest or from the Helm chart, and the other says that no supported deployment or GitOps path consumes the generated files. Beside the new claim, each would contradict the register.
findings.resolution: A dated note is appended to each limitation. Both claims stay planned and cite no record: one run on one provider with one contract does not establish either general statement.

findings.observation: The claims of the two static runs each say, in what they do not establish, that E01-D 'has not run'. The evidence record of each says the same. E01-D ran once on 2026-10-06.
findings.resolution: The clause is replaced in the second static run's claim. The review gate allows that change, because a review record of that run exists and this ledger references it. The same clause in the first static run's claim is not changed: no review record of run 20261002-e01-abc-1 exists, the review gate refuses a change to that claim without one, and this change creates no review. The two evidence records are dated records of their runs and are not changed. The first claim's clause and both records' sentences therefore still say that E01-D has not run, and they describe the state when each run was recorded.

findings.observation: The register's reason for the evidence index, a surface that claims nothing, named nine ledgers of register changes. This ledger is a tenth, and the released pack is recomputed by undoing it too.
findings.resolution: The reason is replaced; the surface claims nothing.

codeRevisions.note: The run manifest names the commit it executed. It records that git status printed no line before the run, that refs/heads/main on the remote named that commit, and that Argo CD reported the same commit as the synced revision. The API image was built at that commit, with every layer taken from the build cache.
